topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the course, and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer causation, environmental exposures, and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Intrinsic Mutation Risk, Environmental Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic disease driven by a combination of endogenous mutations, genetic predispositions, and geographical and lifestyle variations revealed through epidemiology.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Burkitt Lymphoma in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens promote malignancy, using the epidemiological and molecular case study of Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate viral-driven oncogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review various dietary, environmental, and tobacco-related carcinogens—such as aflatoxin, UV light, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and aromatic amines—and explain how they are metabolized to cause DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Developmental Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on the distinction between tumor initiators and promoters, the role of chronic inflammation, and how tissue proliferative states influence cancer susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and conclude with considerations of exposure dose, potency, and risk-benefit trade-offs.
